title: Branch Office, Liaison Office or Project Office: Choosing a Route Into India
seo_title: Branch vs Liaison vs Project Office in India
meta_description: Branch, liaison and project offices compared for a foreign company entering India: permitted work, the RBI approval route, and which fits your plan.
intro: A foreign company that wants a direct, unincorporated presence in India, rather than setting up an Indian subsidiary, has three options under the foreign exchange rules: a liaison office, a branch office or a project office. Each is opened under the same regulatory scheme, needs the Reserve Bank of India's approval routed through an authorised bank, and carries a different, fixed set of activities it may undertake. Picking the wrong one is a common and avoidable mistake, because converting from one to another later is not a simple formality.

The choice turns on what the foreign company actually wants to do in India. A liaison office is a listening post with no commercial activity at all. A branch office can trade, invoice and earn income, but only within a defined list of activities. A project office exists for one contract and closes when that contract ends. This guide sets out the differences as they stand today, the approval process, and the points a foreign parent's board should settle before an application goes in.

sections.heading: What each office is actually allowed to do
paragraphs: A liaison office, sometimes called a representative office, may only act as a channel of communication between the foreign head office and parties in India. It can represent the parent, promote its products, give information about the parent to prospective Indian customers and pass information back about Indian market conditions. What it cannot do is earn any income in India. Every expense of a liaison office has to be met by remittances from the parent abroad, and that distinction is checked closely by the authorised dealer bank each time the office renews its approval.

A branch office sits at the other end of the spectrum. It is allowed to carry out the activities permitted for the foreign company under its own memorandum, within a list the regulation sets out, which includes export and import of goods, rendering professional or consultancy services, carrying out research work in areas the parent is engaged in, and acting as a buying or selling agent. A branch office is not permitted to carry out manufacturing or processing activities in India directly, although it may subcontract these to an Indian manufacturer, and it cannot engage in retail trading of any kind.

A project office sits in between. It is set up solely to execute a specific project the foreign company has been awarded in India, typically a contract from an Indian company, and its permission is tied to that contract's duration. Once the project is complete, the office is expected to wind up and remit any surplus, subject to tax clearance. A project office can do only what the underlying contract requires, so a company that wants an ongoing India presence beyond one project should not use this route.

sections.heading: The approval route and who decides it
paragraphs: All three types of office are opened under the regulations framed by the Reserve Bank of India under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, and the application is made through an authorised dealer category-I bank, not directly to the RBI. Where the foreign company's principal business falls in a sector where 100 per cent foreign direct investment is not permitted under the automatic route, or where the applicant is a non-government organisation, a non-profit, a body or an agency, or is from certain countries that require extra scrutiny, the application is referred by the bank to the RBI, which considers it along with the government where needed.

For a project office, there is a separate and somewhat easier route where the contract has already been secured from an Indian company and funded in a specified way, such as by inward remittance from abroad or by a loan from a public financial institution or bank in India; in that case, the office can generally be set up through the authorised dealer bank without a separate RBI reference. On approval, a branch or project office is given a unique identification number, and all three types of office must register with the Registrar of Companies as a place of business of a foreign company and file the annual returns that requirement carries.

sections.heading: Tax exposure is different for each, and that should drive the choice
paragraphs: A liaison office, if it genuinely confines itself to communication and does not conclude contracts or negotiate on the parent's behalf in India, is generally treated as not creating a taxable presence in India for the foreign company. The moment it starts doing anything closer to a branch office's work, even informally, tax authorities have in practice argued that it has created a business connection or a permanent establishment, which exposes the foreign parent's India-linked income to Indian tax. This is the most common way liaison offices run into trouble, and it is usually self-inflicted by staff who start negotiating deals instead of merely introducing parties.

A branch office, because it can earn income, is taxed in India as a foreign company at the rate applicable to foreign companies, which is materially different from the rate an Indian subsidiary would pay, and it does not get the deductions and set-offs available to a domestic company. A project office is taxed on the income attributable to the specific project, and its wind-up requires a tax clearance certificate before the final remittance of any surplus abroad, which in practice takes time and should be planned for well before the contract is expected to end.

sections.heading: Property, staffing and banking
paragraphs: A branch office or a project office may acquire property in India for its own use and to carry out its permitted activities, but not to lease it out to anyone else. A liaison office cannot acquire property at all and must operate from leased premises, with the lease period generally kept within five years under the general permission available for this purpose. All three types of office can open a current account with their authorised dealer bank in India once approval is granted, but none of them can open any other kind of account, borrow in India in the ordinary course, or guarantee a loan to an Indian entity.

Staffing has its own layer of compliance that is easy to overlook. Expatriate staff posted to a liaison, branch or project office need the right visa category and, in most cases, registration with the local Foreigners Regional Registration Office once their stay in India crosses the applicable threshold, and the office has its own set of labour law obligations toward any locally hired staff, which do not disappear simply because the entity has no separate Indian corporate personality.

sections.heading: Renewal, extension and what happens if the company wants to change course
paragraphs: A liaison office's approval is not indefinite. It is typically granted for a period and must be renewed before expiry, and the authorised dealer bank reviews the office's activities each time to confirm it has stayed within the liaison-only mandate. A branch office's approval tends to run with the underlying business activity and is reviewed periodically in a similar way. A project office's life is tied to the project; if the project is extended, the office's permission needs to be extended with it, and if the contract is terminated early, the office has to close and remit funds with the same tax clearance step.

If a foreign company that started with a liaison office later wants to do commercial business in India, it cannot simply convert the liaison office into a branch office by notifying the bank. In practice this means applying afresh for a branch office or, more commonly, incorporating an Indian subsidiary and winding down the liaison office separately. Because of this, companies that are fairly confident they will want to trade in India within a year or two are often better served going straight to a branch office application, or to a subsidiary, rather than starting with a liaison office and having to redo the exercise later.

None of the three routes gives the foreign company a separate Indian legal personality. The head office abroad remains directly liable for everything the Indian office does, which is the main reason most groups that expect a lasting, growing India presence eventually move to an Indian subsidiary once the initial market-testing phase is over, keeping the branch or liaison office only for the narrow purpose it was approved for in the meantime.

faqs.q: Can a liaison office sign contracts on behalf of its foreign parent in India?
faqs.a: No. A liaison office exists only to pass information between the foreign head office and parties in India. Negotiating or signing contracts, raising invoices, or otherwise conducting business crosses into branch office territory and risks both a FEMA violation and an Indian tax exposure for the parent that the liaison structure was meant to avoid.

faqs.q: Is RBI approval always required to open a branch or liaison office?
faqs.a: Yes, all three types of office need approval routed through an authorised dealer category-I bank under the regulations framed by the Reserve Bank of India. Whether the file is cleared by the bank itself or referred to the RBI depends on the applicant's sector, structure and country of incorporation.

faqs.q: Can a project office undertake work beyond the contract it was set up for?
faqs.a: No. A project office's permission is tied to the specific contract that justified its approval. Taking on unrelated work through the same office is outside its mandate; a separate approval, or a different structure such as a branch office or subsidiary, is needed for any activity beyond that project.

faqs.q: How long does it typically take to wind up a branch, liaison or project office?
faqs.a: Closure needs a tax clearance certificate before any surplus funds can be remitted abroad, along with closure of the current account and surrender of the registration with the Registrar of Companies. Because the tax clearance step depends on the assessing authority's timeline, companies should start the closure process well before they need the funds back.

Permitted activities for each office type (liaison = communication channel only; branch = list including export/import, consultancy, R&D, no retail trading or manufacturing; project office tied to one contract): confirmed from the RBI's own FAQ page on Branch/Liaison/Project offices and from the RBI Master Direction/FEMA 22(R) regulation text; both are primary RBI sources.

Approval route through an AD Category-I bank, with RBI/government reference depending on sector and applicant type: confirmed from the RBI FAQ page and corroborated by secondary commentary (EY, Mondaq, taxguru) summarising the same regulation.
Property acquisition allowed for BO/PO but not LO, and the five-year general permission for leased premises: confirmed directly from the RBI FAQ page on this subject.
